findings.title: Executable annotation arguments are excluded from Python payload indexing and leak through a mirrored annotation
rules: SPEC0209 implementation/body prohibition and UNKNOWN provenance

locations.role: Annotation and return fields skipped wholesale by runtime_literals
Dynamic annotation loses literals; mirrored string is unparsed without collision evidence
Connected Python extraction and catalog emission

inert_witness.application: Hypothetical replacement of python/sdk/src/sdk.py in the sealed synthetic fixture; do not execute.

expected.parameter_type: UNKNOWN with reason and payload digest/length
expected.return_type: UNKNOWN with reason and payload digest/length
expected.requirements: Keep python-surface and run entries, source digest, P100-025 ownership, original IDs and NOT_VERIFIED parity

source_level_derivation: The complete witness contains an explicit built-in eval call in an annotation and has no binding that shadows eval. Its argument is executable Python expression source. No execution or cross-file resolution is needed to identify this source role.

runtime_literals visits FunctionDef.args but skips ast.arg.annotation; it also skips FunctionDef.returns (994). It therefore never indexes either string and produces an empty payload_literals set for this witness.
typ of the parameter sees ast.Call, fails its allowed-node test (1006-1007), and returns only the generic UNKNOWN above, without a digest/length.
typ of the return sees an allowed ast.Constant string, finds no collision (1010), and returns ast.unparse(n) at 1012: the exact string representation shown above.

sig and the python-function row (1013-1028) transport that return string through the Python result to emitFor. Identity projection affects symbol only; neither it nor validateCatalog redacts shape. The source contributes two entries (python-surface and python-function), and the run entry remains UNKNOWN but still copies the payload.

test_gap.assessment: Tests cover ordinary runtime calls and dynamic annotation/base rejection separately. The dynamic-annotation fixture also repeats its marker in a base/body, so it does not test a runtime source literal whose sole runtime occurrence is inside an annotation. Tests were read, never run.

findings.action: Traverse runtime expression descendants inside dynamic annotation/return nodes for source-local payload evidence while preserving genuine declaration-only strings. Retain literal provenance on dynamic UNKNOWN projections, then cover this same-source mirror without executing eval.
findings.confidence: Source-level control/data-flow derivation only; no observed execution result.

findings.title: JSON $ref bypasses existing same-source payload collision evidence
rules: B-genuine-literal-selector: unresolved dual role stays UNKNOWN

locations.role: $ref OR branch omits payloadLiterals collision check
Physical Markdown prepass and connected JSON/TypeScript projection

inert_witness.application: Hypothetical replacement of docs/tool-catalog.md in the sealed synthetic fixture; never construct a Worker.

$ref.reason: Unresolved executable payload / declaration locator role; bytes not copied

expected.requirements: Retain document-type, document-json and document-surface entries, all source/owner fields, stable identities and NOT_VERIFIED parity

type.reason: Unclassified literal in a declared type; bytes not copied

source_level_derivation: /C_ROUTE/ is an inert example of valid JavaScript program source (a regexp expression statement), explicitly supplied as Worker source with eval:true. The audit does not execute it.
The Markdown prepass parses the recognized TS fence and indexRuntimeLiterals records the Worker argument (1332-1339,735-770), skipping only the type representation. All fences share that same map.
The TypeScript Mirror becomes UNKNOWN via printed (557-582), demonstrating the collision is already known to the connected extraction.

The JSON projection receives the map (1431-1436). $ref is a known vocabulary member (1048,1130-1154). Its string passes the $ref regexp at 1223. That disjunct lacks the !payloadLiterals.has(hash(value)) condition used for name/required at 1222, so 1225 returns the raw string despite the known collision.

The context Contracts/Locator is identityVocabulary-compatible and does not contain the payload. Both identity projections leave it unchanged. emitFor copies the shape, marks it STATIC because no UNKNOWN remains there, retains P100-003/source SHA and NOT_VERIFIED parity, and validateCatalog accepts the internally consistent shape. Three document entries remain.

test_gap.assessment: Tests cover same-source TS/JSON sharing and JSON name collisions, but not $ref collisions. The current $ref branch is visibly different from name/required.

findings.action: Require collision clearance for the $ref vocabulary branch, retaining UNKNOWN reason/hash/length when the role is unresolved. Add a direct connected Markdown regression for an already-indexed payload mirrored into $ref; preserve genuine locator-only declarations.
findings.confidence: Exact source-level branch derivation; no helper or fixture execution.

findings.title: Genuine quoted ambient module selectors lose their exact declaration spelling
rules: SPEC0209 declaration/contract shape retention; no identity migration required

locations.role: nodeName makes quoted names with spaces opaque
Module name used only as projected context; child shape lacks exact enclosing selector
Final identity projection retains only digest-based identity

inert_witness.application: Hypothetical replacement of packages/core/example/src/types.ts in the sealed synthetic fixture; declaration only.
inert_witness.text: declare module "opaque module one" { export const asset: number; }

findings.expected: Keep existing opaque IDs/symbol projection, but preserve the exact authenticated ambient module selector in inert declaration metadata. No payload collision exists; whitespace is not a reason to discard genuine contract spelling.

derived_output.raw_symbol_formula: canonicalJSON(opaqueLiteral("opaque module one", "Unclassified literal name; bytes not copied")) + ".asset"
derived_output.identity_projection_formula: opaqueLiteral(raw_symbol, "Unclassified identity text; stable digest replaces literal bytes")

source_level_derivation: The static ModuleDeclaration string is a genuine external-module contract selector. There are no runtime expressions or unclassified payloads in the witness.

indexRuntimeLiterals excludes declaration names, leaving the payload index empty. Nevertheless nodeName applies identityVocabulary to the quoted module name (590-593); the space fails the regular expression at 20, so only its digest/length/reason is returned.
visitStatements canonicalizes that object into the module symbol and constructs the child prefix at 802-811. It emits no module record or declared_name/context field for the module selector.

The public asset declaration emits type:number and value:UNKNOWN Initializer absent (893-911). Its raw symbol contains the opaque parent object, not the original selector. Any generic name_resolution UNKNOWN added at 785-794 likewise carries no original spelling.

emitFor projectIdentity hashes the punctuation-containing raw symbol and adds identity_projection with another digest/length. Neither the value shape, symbol, source path, nor the separate source hash preserves the selector text. There are two entries (value plus source-surface); no requirement deletion or ID migration is needed to repair the lost declaration metadata.

test_gap.assessment: The opaque-module test checks distinct entries/IDs/UNKNOWN only. It never asserts exact module-selector preservation. Quoted event/class names receive declared_name metadata elsewhere, illustrating a compatible remedy while retaining opaque identities.

findings.action: Carry the exact authenticated quoted module selector in declaration context metadata when no same-source payload collision exists; leave opaque IDs unchanged. Add positive space/punctuation/module-selector cases and collision negatives.
findings.confidence: Static derivation; no TypeScript parsing/execution performed by the auditor.
